name: Watsco, Inc.
moat_justification: Largest North American HVAC/R distributor (~685+ locations, 125,000+ contractors, estimated high-teens share of a fragmented $74B market) with scale purchasing power, local availability and a scaling digital ecosystem (e-commerce 37% of sales); ROIC proxy stayed 20-34% over the last five fiscal years and never below 17% in ten, and gross margin expanded from 24.2% (2020) to a record 28.0% (2025) — but it sells other makers' products into a still-fragmented field of ~1,400-2,200 distributors, so the moat is strong, not wide.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 10 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
TIER_BAND: bear-case tier D (6.6%) vs bull-case tier C (10.5%) — the verdict spans tiers; size any position to the bear end
one_liner: High-quality compounder, moat 7/10 — but at $295.91 it does not clear 15% on any defensible base (weighted IRR 8.1% on the TTM base, 6.9% on the median base; IV@15% $133.56); it clears 15% only at or below ~$134.
moat_for: Scale: largest HVAC/R distributor in North America, estimated 18-20% share vs ~$3B-revenue next rivals, 685+ locations and 125,000+ contractors
ROIC proxy 20.3-34.0% over FY2021-25 and 17-21% in FY2016-20 — above cost of capital through the whole cycle
Pricing power proven: gross margin 24.2% (2020) to record 28.0% (2025) via pricing-optimization technology, expanded even as 2025 volumes fell
Digital lock-in: e-commerce +13% in H1 2026 at 37% of trailing sales, OnCallAir $1.9B GMV — tools small distributors cannot match
Replacement-driven demand (residential replacement is the core) plus a debt-light balance sheet funding 70+ buy-and-build acquisitions since 1989
moat_against: No proprietary product — distributes OEM equipment (Carrier and others); OEM concentration and direct/OEM-channel shifts are a standing hostage risk
Market remains fragmented (~1,400-2,200 distributors); local availability moats erode branch by branch and price competition is constant in commodity segments
Gross margin is only 27-28% and the 2025 record leaned on OEM/A2L pricing actions that reversed in Q2 2026 (27.5% vs 29.3%)
Housing and consumer-durables cyclicality: FY2025 revenue fell 5% on A2L-transition volume softness and slower homebuilding
Share count creeps up ~1.7%/yr with no buyback offset and the dividend absorbs essentially all earnings, leaving little reinvestment cushion
